1:1: It came to pass, when the children of Israel were taken captive by the king of the Chaldeans, that God spoke to Jeremiah: Jeremiah, my chosen one, arise, go out of this city, you and Baruch; for I am going to destroy it because of the multitude of the sins of those who dwell in it.
1:2: For your prayers are like a firm pillar in the midst of it, and like an unbreakable wall surrounding it.
1:3: Now arise and go out, before the army of the Chaldeans surrounds it.
1:4: And Jeremiah answered, saying: I beseech you, Lord, permit me, your servant, to speak before you. And the Lord said to him:
1:5: Speak, my chosen one Jeremiah. And Jeremiah spoke, saying: Lord Almighty, are you handing over the chosen city into the hands of the Chaldeans, so that the king may boast with the multitude of his people and say, I have prevailed over the holy city of God?
1:6: No, my Lord; but if it is your will, let it be destroyed by your own hands.
1:7: And the Lord said to Jeremiah: Since you are my chosen one, arise and go out of this city, you and Baruch; for I am going to destroy it because of the multitude of the sins of those who dwell in it.
1:8: For neither the king nor his army will be able to enter it unless I first open its gates.
1:9: Arise then, and go to Baruch, and tell him these words.
1:10: And arise at the sixth hour of the night and come out onto the walls of the city, and I will show you that unless I first destroy the city, they cannot enter it.
1:11: When the Lord had said this, he departed from Jeremiah.
2:1: And Jeremiah tore his garments and put dust on his head, and went into the sanctuary of God. And when Baruch saw him with dust sprinkled on his head and his garments torn, he cried out with a loud voice, saying: Father Jeremiah, what is the matter with you? Or what sin
2:4: For whenever the people sinned, Jeremiah would sprinkle dust on his head and pray for the people until their sin was forgiven them.
2:5: And Baruch asked him, saying: Father, what is the matter with you? And Jeremiah said to him:
2:6: Beware of tearing your garments; rather let us tear our hearts. And let us not draw water for the troughs, but let us weep and fill them with tears; for the Lord will not have mercy on this people. And Baruch said: Father Jeremiah, what has happened?
2:7: And Jeremiah said: God is handing the city over into the hands of the king of the Chaldeans, to take the people captive to Babylon.
2:8: When Baruch heard this, he too tore his garments and said: Father Jeremiah, who made this known to you?
2:9: And Jeremiah said to him: Wait with me a little, until the sixth hour of the night, so that you may know that the word is true.
2:10: So they remained at the altar, weeping.
3:1: And when the hour of the night came, as the Lord had told Jeremiah, Jeremiah and Baruch went up together onto the walls of the city.
3:2: And there was a sound of trumpets, and angels came out of heaven holding torches in their hands, and they stood on the walls of the city.
3:3: When Jeremiah and Baruch saw them, they wept, saying: Now we know that the word is true.
3:4: And Jeremiah besought the angels, saying: I beseech you, do not destroy the city yet, until I say a word to the Lord. And the Lord said to the angels: Do not destroy the city until I speak to my chosen one Jeremiah. And Jeremiah said: I pray you, Lord, bid me speak before you.
3:5: And the Lord said: Speak, my chosen one Jeremiah.
3:6: And Jeremiah said: Behold, Lord, now we know that you are handing your city over into the hands of its enemies, and they will carry the people away to Babylon. What shall we do with your holy things, the vessels of your service? What do you want us to do with them?
3:8: And the Lord said to him: Take them and give them over to the earth and to the altar, saying: Hear, O earth, the voice of him who created you in the abundance of the waters, who sealed you with seven seals in seven periods, and after this you will receive your beauty: guard the vessels of the service until the gathering of the beloved. And Jeremiah spoke:
3:9: I beseech you, Lord, show me what I shall do for Abimelech the Ethiopian, for he did many kindnesses to the people and to your servant Jeremiah, for he drew me up out of the miry pit; and I do not want him to see the destruction and desolation of the city, but that he should not be grieved.
3:10: And the Lord said to Jeremiah: Send him to the vineyard of Agrippa by the mountain road, and I will shelter him until I bring the people back to the city.
3:11: And the Lord said to Jeremiah: Go with your people to Babylon, and stay with them, preaching the good news to them, until I bring them back to the city.
3:12: But leave Baruch here until I speak with him.
3:13: When the Lord had said this, he went up from Jeremiah into heaven.
3:14: And Jeremiah and Baruch went into the sanctuary, and they gave the vessels of the service over to the earth, as the Lord had told them; and at once the earth swallowed them up. And the two sat down and wept.
3:15: When morning came, Jeremiah sent Abimelech away, saying: Take the basket and go to the estate of Agrippa by the mountain road, and bring a few figs, and give them to the sick among the people; for the favour of the Lord is upon you, and glory is upon your head.
3:16: And he went off as he had told him.
4:1: When morning came, behold, the army of the Chaldeans surrounded the city; and the great angel sounded the trumpet, saying: Enter the city, army of the Chaldeans; for behold, the gate has been opened for you.
4:2: So the king entered with his multitude, and they took all the people captive.
4:3: But Jeremiah took the keys of the temple, went outside the city, and threw them before the sun, saying: I say to you, sun, take the keys of the temple of God and guard them until the day on which the Lord will ask you about them.
4:4: For we were not found worthy to guard them, because we became false stewards.
4:5: While Jeremiah was still weeping for the people, they were dragged away to Babylon.
4:6: But Baruch put dust on his head and sat down and wept this lament, saying: Why has Jerusalem been laid waste? Because of the sins of the beloved people she was handed over into the hands of enemies, because of our sins and the sins of the people. But let not the lawless boast and say, We were strong enough to take the city of God by our own might. You did prevail over it, but it was because of our sins that we were handed over.
4:8: But our God will have mercy on us and will bring us back to our city; but you will not have life.
4:9: Blessed are our fathers, Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, for they went out of this world and did not see the destruction of this city.
4:10: When he had said this, he went out, weeping and saying: Grieving for you, Jerusalem, I have gone out from you. And he stayed sitting in a tomb, while the angels came and told him about everything.
5:1: Now Abimelech carried the figs in the heat; and coming upon a tree, he sat down under its shade to rest a little. And leaning his head on the basket of figs, he fell asleep, and slept for sixty-six years; and he did not wake from his sleep.
5:2: And afterwards, when he woke from his sleep, he said: I would gladly have slept a little longer, for my head is heavy, because I have not had enough of my sleep. And uncovering the basket of figs, he found them dripping milk.
5:4: And he said: I would like to sleep
5:5: a little, for my head is heavy; but I am afraid that I may fall asleep and be late in waking, and Jeremiah my father may think little of me; for if he were not in a hurry, he would not have sent me at dawn today.
5:6: So I will get up and go on in the heat; for is there not heat and toil every day? So he got up and took the basket of figs and put it on his shoulders, and went into Jerusalem; and he did not recognise it, neither his house, nor the place, nor his own family. And he said:
5:8: Blessed be the Lord, for a great bewilderment has come upon me. This is not
5:9: the city; I have lost my way, because I came by the mountain road,
5:10: having got up from my sleep; and because my head was heavy, since I had not had enough of my sleep, I have lost my way.
5:11: It will seem a marvel to say this before Jeremiah, that I lost my way.
5:12: And he went out of the city; and looking closely, he saw the landmarks of the city, and said: This is indeed the city; yet I have lost my way.
5:13: And again he went back into the city and searched, and found none of his own people.
5:14: And he said: Blessed be the Lord, for a great bewilderment has come upon me.
5:15: And again he went outside the city. And he stayed there grieving, not knowing where to go.
5:16: And he put down the basket, saying: I will sit here until the Lord takes this bewilderment from me.
5:17: And as he sat, he saw an old man coming from the field; and Abimelech said to him: I say to you, old man, what city is this?
5:18: And he said to him: It is Jerusalem. And Abimelech said to him: Where is Jeremiah the priest, and Baruch the reader, and all the people of this city? For I have not found them.
5:19: And the old man said to him: Are you not
5:20: from this city, that you remember Jeremiah today and ask about him after so long a time?
5:21: For Jeremiah is in Babylon with the people; for they were taken captive by King Nebuchadnezzar, and Jeremiah is with them
5:22: to preach the good news to them and to teach them the word. As soon as
5:23: Abimelech heard this from the old man, he said: If you were not an old man, and if it were not unlawful for a man to insult one older than himself, I would laugh at you and say that you are mad, since you said, The people have been taken captive to Babylon.
5:24: Even if the cataracts of heaven had come down on them, there has not yet been time to go to Babylon.
5:25: For how long is it since my father Jeremiah sent me to the estate of Agrippa for a few figs, so that we might give them to the sick among the
5:26: people? And I went and brought them; and coming to a certain tree in the heat, I sat down to rest a little, and leaned my head on the basket, and fell asleep; and when I woke I uncovered the basket of figs, thinking that I was late, and I found the figs dripping milk, just as I had gathered them. And you say that the people have been taken captive to Babylon?
5:27: But so that you may know, take them, look at the figs.
5:28: And he uncovered the basket of figs for the old man.
5:29: And he saw them dripping milk. And when he saw them,
5:30: the old man said: O my son, you are a righteous man, and God did not want to show you the desolation of the city; for God brought this bewilderment upon you. For behold, it is sixty-six years today since the people were taken captive to Babylon.
5:31: And so that you may learn, child, that it is true, look up at the field and see that the growth of the crops has appeared; see the figs too, that it is not their season, and know it.
5:32: Then Abimelech cried out with a loud voice, saying: I will bless you, Lord, God of heaven and earth, the rest of the souls of the righteous in every place.
5:33: And he said to the old man: What month is this? And he said: Nisan, and it is the twelfth.
5:34: And taking some of the figs, he gave them to the old man, and said to him: May God guide you with his light to the city above
6:1: After this Abimelech went outside the city and prayed to the Lord. And behold, an angel of the Lord came and set him down where Baruch was; and he found him sitting in a tomb.
6:2: And when they saw each other, they both wept and kissed each other. And Baruch looked up and saw the figs covered in the basket; and lifting his eyes to heaven, he prayed, saying: There is a God who gives a reward to his holy ones.
6:3: Prepare yourself, my heart, and be glad, and rejoice in your tabernacle, I mean your fleshly house; for your mourning has been turned into joy. For the Mighty One is coming and will take you out of your tabernacle; for no sin has been found in you.
6:4: Be refreshed, my virgin faith, and believe that you will live.
6:5: Look at this basket of figs: behold, they have been sixty-six years, and they have not withered nor gone sour, but they drip with milk. So it will be with my flesh, if you do what you are commanded by the angel of righteousness.
6:7: He who kept the basket of figs will keep you again by his power.
6:8: When Baruch had said this, he said to Abimelech: Arise, and let us pray that the Lord may make known to us how we can send the message to Jeremiah in Babylon about the shelter that was given you.
6:9: And Baruch prayed, saying: Our strength, our God, Lord, the chosen light that came out of his mouth, I beseech and implore your goodness; the great name which no one can
6:10: know: hear the voice of your servant, and let knowledge come into my heart. What do you want us to do? How shall I send to Jeremiah in Babylon?
6:11: And while Baruch was still praying,
6:12: behold, an angel of the Lord came and said to Baruch: Baruch, counsellor of the light, do not be anxious about how to send to Jeremiah; for an eagle is coming to you tomorrow at the hour of light, and you will send word by it to Jeremiah.
6:13: Write then in the letter: Speak to the children of Israel:
6:14: Whoever has become a stranger among you, let him be set apart, and let them keep fifteen days; and after this I will bring you into your city, says the Lord.
6:15: Whoever is not set apart from Babylon, O Jeremiah, shall not enter the city; and I rebuke them, so that they will not be received again by the Babylonians, says the Lord.
6:16: And when the angel had said this, he departed from Baruch.
6:17: And Baruch sent to the market of the Gentiles and got paper and ink, and wrote
6:18: a letter that read as follows: Baruch the servant of God writes to Jeremiah, who is in the captivity of Babylon: Rejoice and be glad, for God has not let us depart from this body grieving for the city that was laid waste and outraged.
6:19: Therefore the Lord has had compassion on our tears, and has remembered the covenant that he established with our fathers Abraham, Isaac and Jacob.
6:20: For he sent his angel to me, and he told me these words which I have sent to you.
6:21: These, then, are the words which the Lord, the God of Israel, spoke, who brought us out of the land of Egypt, out of the
6:22: great furnace: Because you did not keep my ordinances, but your heart was lifted up and you were stiff-necked before me, I was angry, and in wrath I handed you over to the furnace in Babylon.
6:23: If then you listen to my voice, says the Lord, from the mouth of Jeremiah my servant, whoever listens I will bring up out of Babylon; but whoever does not listen will become a stranger to Jerusalem and to Babylon.
6:24: And you will test them by the water of the Jordan; whoever does not listen will be made plain. This is the sign of the great seal.
7:1: And Baruch got up and went out of the tomb.
7:2: And the eagle answered with a human voice and said: Greetings, Baruch, steward of the faith.
7:3: And Baruch said to him: You who speak are chosen out of all the birds of heaven; for it is plain from the brightness of your eyes.
7:4: Show me, then, what you are doing here.
7:5: And the eagle said to him: I was sent here so that you might send by me whatever message you wish.
7:6: And Baruch said to him: Can you carry this message to Jeremiah in Babylon?
7:7: And the eagle said to him: It was for this that I was sent.
7:8: And Baruch took the letter and fifteen figs from Abimelech's basket, and tied them to the eagle's neck, and said to him:
7:9: I say to you, king of the birds, go in peace and in good health, and bring the message back to me.
7:10: Do not be like the raven which Noah sent out, and which never came back to him in the ark; but be like the dove, which the third time brought back word to the righteous man. So you too, take this good message to Jeremiah and to those with him, that it may go well with you; take this paper to the chosen people of God.
7:12: If all the birds of heaven surround you, and all the enemies of the truth want to fight with you, struggle: the Lord will give you strength. And do not turn aside to the right or to the left, but go straight like an arrow; so go in the power of God.
7:13: Then the eagle flew off with the letter and went to Babylon, and rested on a tree outside the city in a deserted place; and it kept silent until
7:14: Jeremiah passed by, he and some others of the people; for they were going out to bury a dead man. For Jeremiah had asked Nebuchadnezzar, saying: Give me a place where I may bury the dead of my people.
7:15: And he gave it to him. And as they went along weeping with the dead man, they came opposite the eagle; and the eagle cried out, saying: I say to you, Jeremiah, chosen one of God, go, gather all the people, and let them come here, so that they may hear the good news which I have brought you from Baruch and Abimelech.
7:16: When Jeremiah heard this, he glorified God; and he went and gathered the people with their wives and children, and came to where the eagle was.
7:17: And the eagle came down on the dead man, and he came back to life. This happened so that they might believe.
7:18: And all the people marvelled at what had happened, saying: Is not this the God who appeared to our fathers in the wilderness through Moses, and who has made himself in the form of an eagle and appeared to us through this great eagle?
7:19: And the eagle said to Jeremiah: Come, untie this letter and read it to the people.
7:20: So he untied the letter and read it to the people. And when the people heard it, they wept and put dust on their heads, and
7:21: said to Jeremiah: Save us, and tell us what we must do to enter our city again.
7:22: And Jeremiah answered and said to them: All that you have heard from the letter,
7:23: keep it, and he will bring us into our city. And Jeremiah also wrote a letter to Baruch, saying thus: My beloved son, do not be negligent in your prayers, interceding for us, that he may prosper our way until we come out from under the decrees of this lawless king; for you were found righteous before him, and he did not let you come here with us, so that you would not see the affliction which has come upon the people at the hands of the
7:24: Babylonians. For it is as with a father who has an only son, and this son is handed over to punishment: those who see his father and comfort him cover his face, so that he may not see how his son is being punished and be the more wasted by grief. So God has had mercy on you and did not let you come to Babylon, so that you would not see the affliction of the people. For since we came into this city, grief has not left us, sixty-six years today.
7:25: For often when I went out I found some of the people hanged by King Nebuchadnezzar, weeping and saying: Have mercy on us, O god Zar.
7:26: Hearing this, I grieved and wept a double weeping, not only because they were hanged, but because they called on a foreign god, saying: Have mercy on us. And I remembered the feast days that we kept in Jerusalem before we were taken captive.
7:27: And remembering, I groaned, and returned to my house in pain and weeping.
7:28: Now then, pray in the place where you are, you and Abimelech, for this people, that they may listen to my voice and to the judgments of my mouth, and that we may go out from here.
7:29: For I tell you that the whole time we have spent here, they have held us, saying: Sing us a song from the songs of Zion, the song of your God. And we answered them: How shall we sing to you, being in a foreign land?
7:30: And after this he tied the letter to the eagle's neck, saying: Go in peace, and may the Lord watch over us both.
7:31: And the eagle flew off and carried the letter and gave it to Baruch. And he untied it and read it, and kissed it, and wept when he heard of the griefs and afflictions of the people.
7:32: And Jeremiah took the figs and distributed them to the sick among the people. And he went on teaching them to keep away from the pollutions of the Gentiles of Babylon.
8:1: And the day came on which God brought the people out of Babylon; and the Lord said to Jeremiah:
8:2: Arise, you and the people, and come to the Jordan, and you shall say to the people: Whoever wants the Lord, let him leave behind the works of Babylon, both the men who have taken wives from them and the women who have taken husbands from them.
8:3: And let those who listen to you cross over, and take them up to Jerusalem; but those who do not listen to you, do not bring them into it.
8:4: And Jeremiah spoke these words to them; and they arose and came to the Jordan to cross over, and he told them the words which the Lord had spoken to him. And half of those who had married among them would not listen to Jeremiah, but said to him: We will never leave our wives; but we will bring them back with us to our city.
8:5: So they crossed the Jordan and came to Jerusalem. And Jeremiah stood, with Baruch and Abimelech, saying: No one who has fellowship with the Babylonians shall enter this city. And they said to one another: Let us arise and go back to Babylon, to our own place.
8:7: And they set out. But when they came to Babylon, the Babylonians came out to meet them, saying: You shall not enter our city, because you hated us and went out from us secretly; therefore you shall not come in to us. For we have bound one another with an oath by the name of our god to receive neither you nor your children, since you went out from us secretly.
8:8: And when they learned this, they turned back, and came to a deserted place far from Jerusalem, and built themselves a city, and called its name Samaria.
8:9: And Jeremiah sent to them, saying: Repent; for an angel of righteousness is coming, and he will bring you into your place on high.
9:1: And those with Jeremiah remained, rejoicing and offering sacrifice for the people for nine days.
9:2: And on the tenth day Jeremiah
9:3: alone offered sacrifice, and prayed a prayer, saying: Holy, holy, holy, the incense of the living trees, the true light that enlightens me until I am taken up to you; for the sweet voice of the two seraphim,
9:4: I pray for another sweet fragrance of incense;
9:5: and my meditation is Michael, the archangel of righteousness, until he brings the righteous in.
9:6: I beseech you, Lord Almighty of all creation, unbegotten and incomprehensible, in whom all judgment was hidden before these things came to be.
9:7: While Jeremiah was saying this, standing at the altar with Baruch and Abimelech, he became like one of those
9:8: who gives up his soul. And Baruch and Abimelech stayed there weeping and crying out with a loud voice: Our father Jeremiah, the priest of God, has left us and gone away.
9:9: And all the people heard their weeping, and they all ran to them, and saw Jeremiah lying on the ground dead; and they tore their garments and put dust on their heads and wept bitterly.
9:10: And after this they prepared themselves to bury him. And behold, a voice came, saying: Do not bury the one who is still living; for his soul is coming back into his body.
9:12: And hearing the voice, they did not bury him, but stayed around his tabernacle for three days, saying and wondering at what hour he would rise.
9:13: And after three days his soul came back into his body, and he lifted up his voice in the midst of them all, and said: Glorify God, all of you glorify God, and the Son of God who wakes us, Jesus Christ, the light of all the ages, the lamp that is not quenched, the life of faith.
9:14: And after these times there will be another four hundred and seventy-seven years, and he comes to the earth; and the tree of life planted in the midst of paradise will make all the unfruitful trees bear fruit, and they will grow and sprout, and
9:15: their fruit will remain with the angels. And the trees that have sprouted and are boastful and say, We have reached our end in the air, he will make them wither with the height of their branches, and will make them be judged, the tree that was set firm. And he will make the scarlet become like white wool. The snow will be made black, the sweet waters will become salt, in the great light of the gladness of God.
9:17: And he will bless the islands so that they bear fruit by the word of the mouth of his Christ.
9:18: For he will come, and go out, and choose for himself twelve apostles, to preach the good news among the nations; he whom I have seen adorned by his Father and coming into the world on the Mount of Olives; and he will fill the hungry souls.
9:19: While Jeremiah was saying this about the Son of God, that he is coming into the world, the people were enraged and said:
9:20: These again are the words spoken by Isaiah the son of Amoz, who said, I have seen God and the Son of God.
9:21: Come, then, let us not kill him by the same death as that one, but let us stone him with stones.
9:22: And Baruch and Abimelech were greatly grieved at this madness, and because they wanted to hear in full the mysteries which he had seen.
9:23: But Jeremiah said to them: Be silent, and do not weep;
9:24: for they will not kill me until I have told you all that I have seen.
9:25: And he said to them: Bring me a stone. And he set it up, and said: Light of the ages, make this stone take on my likeness.
9:26: And the stone took on the likeness of Jeremiah.
9:27: And they stoned the stone, thinking that it was Jeremiah.
9:28: But Jeremiah handed over all the mysteries that he had seen to Baruch and Abimelech.
9:29: And then he stood in the midst of the people, wishing to complete his stewardship.
9:30: And the stone cried out, saying: O foolish children of Israel, why do you stone me, thinking that I am Jeremiah? Behold, Jeremiah is standing in your midst.
9:31: And when they saw him, at once they ran at him with many stones. And his stewardship was fulfilled.
9:32: And Baruch and Abimelech came and buried him, and took the stone and placed it on his tomb, inscribing it thus: This is the stone, the helper of Jeremiah.
